chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Sakhr! Indeed, Allah gives the world to whom He loves and whom He hates, but He does not give this matter (Wilayah) except to the elite of His creation. You, by Allah, are upon my religion and the religion of my forefathers, Ibrahim and Ismail. I do not mean Ali ibn Al-Husayn, nor Muhammad ibn Ali, even though these latter are upon the religion of those former ones.'

key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: The matter, specifically referring to Wilayah or authority
key_terms.صَفْوَتَهُ: His elite, the choicest of His creation

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between worldly provision and spiritual authority (Wilayah) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'Safwah' (elect elite) by contrasting the universal distribution of worldly provision with the exclusive bestowal of Wilayah upon those divinely chosen. He clarifies that while the Imams from the progeny of Ibrahim and Ismail share the core monotheistic faith, their specific authority is a distinct divine appointment rather than a mere consequence of general religious adherence. This distinction underscores the Shia doctrine that spiritual leadership is a specific gift of grace reserved for the purified lineage, separate from the general blessings given to all humanity.
